title: SCIM lease revocation and orphan detection playbook for safe user/group deactivation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers have reported rare but severe cases where SCIM-driven deprovisions (user or group deletions from an IdP) result in accidental hard-deletes in Redwood because of transient IdP glitches or long propagation delays. Current behavior: immediate tombstone/hard-delete after N failed retries or after delta-sync indicates removal. This ticket proposes a playbook and implementation pattern to avoid irreversible user loss while preserving eventual consistency and not overwhelming our backlog processing.

Goals:
- Prevent blind hard-deletes caused by transient idP blips or delta reordering.
- Detect and surface orphaned accounts (created in Redwood but absent in IdP due to sync gaps) for safe remediation.
- Provide deterministic, auditable sequence for lease revocation and final deletion, with clear runbook for operators.
- Keep operational overhead (DLQ size, manual interventions) low and measurable.

High-level approach:
1) Lease-based revocation handshake: when SCIM indicates a delete for a user/group, instead of immediate tombstone we mark a revocation-lease on the resource (lease TTL configurable per customer) and emit an audit event with revocation_token. The IdP connector must ACK the revocation by returning the revocation_token in a follow-up delta or expect explicit confirmation within the lease window.
2) Dual-confirmation for hard-delete: require both (a) confirmed delta from primary IdP that the resource is deleted and (b) absence in two consecutive shadow-syncs (one live delta, one scheduled full scan or snapshot) OR explicit admin confirmation via Console within the lease window before performing irreversible removal.
3) Orphan detection scoring: run a lightweight classifier that combines last_seen (SCIM), last_auth (token activity), and profile attributes to compute orphan_score. If orphan_score > threshold, mark for manual review in the Console instead of auto-delete.
4) Fail-safe DLQ & auto-remediation: transient failures during lease ACK or connector timeouts put the event in a scoped DLQ. A separate remediation worker will retry with backoff and attempt passive confirmation via alternate identity sources (SCIM delta from secondary IdP, SSO login logs). If DLQ age > critical_threshold, surface in Ops dashboard and ping assigned on-call.
5) Runbook & metrics: provide clear operational steps, rollback signals, and SLOs for deprovision workflows.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Stronger safety (dual-confirmation + lease) increases time-to-delete (adds a configurable safety window). Trade-off accepted because customer data loss is higher-impact than slower deprovision.
- Requiring a second confirmation can slightly increase DLQ volume and complexity. Mitigation: compact lease windows for low-risk customers and use heuristics to auto-clear low-orphan_score items.
- Maintaining shadow-syncs (full scans) is more I/O intensive; we will run these at low frequency (daily) and rely primarily on deltas plus one confirmation scan.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- New lease_revocation state added to SCIM resource model and persisted with TTL per-customer.
- Connector updates: IdP adapters emit an ack endpoint and fill revocation_token in subsequent deltas when applicable.
- Dashboard shows "pending revocations", DLQ size, orphan_score distribution, mean time to final delete.
- E2E tests that simulate transient IdP deletion-flapping do not produce hard-deletes; instead items land in "pending_revocation" and either reconcile or surface for manual review.
- Runbook added to Confluence with step-by-step remediation and a sample manual override flow in the Console.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement lease_revocation feature flag and enable for 5 pilot customers; run in read-only shadow mode for 2 weeks to collect metrics.
- Phase 2 (soft-enforce): for pilot customers, require revocation handshake (no hard-delete until dual-confirmation) and enable DLQ remediation worker.
- Phase 3 (global): enable default behavior with per-customer TTL controls and Console admin override; provide migration script for customers with existing tombstoned records.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Deprovision false-positive rate < 0.1% on pilot tenants.
- Mean time from initial SCIM delete to final hard-delete under enforced policy: configurable default 72h for high-safety tenants, 6h for low-safety.
- DLQ remediation queue growth rate tracked and alerting if > 100 items or trend > +25%/day.

Security & audit:
- Every state transition (revocation requested, ack received, shadow-scan confirmed, manual override, final delete) must emit a structured audit log with revocation_token, operator_id, and timestamps.
- Audit logs retained per customer's compliance retention policy and exposed in Console with filters for admin roles.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for lease lifecycle, revocation_token generation, and TTL eviction.
- Integration tests: simulate delta reordering (out-of-order messages), connector timeouts, and IdP resend with revocation_token.
- Chaos test: random network partition between connector and IdP during delete flow; ensure no hard-delete occurs and DLQ behaves as intended.

Open questions:
- Default TTL per customer: propose 24h for standard, 7d for high-safety customers. Ops feedback requested.
- Do we require IdP adapters to always support revocation_token? Fallback: if adapter doesn't support token, rely on dual-shadow confirmation and admin override.
